topic: The Carbon Capture Simulation Initiative (CCSI): Computational Tools To Accelerate Commercial Development
title: The Carbon Capture Simulation Initiative (CCSI): Computational Tools To Accelerate Commercial Development
abstract: The U.S. Department of Energy's Carbon Capture Simulation Initiative (CCSI) is developing, demonstrating and deploying advanced computational tools and models to accelerate the development of next generation technologies, specifically the development of cost effective carbon capture technologies. This CCSI Toolset will (1) enable promising concepts to be evaluated more quickly based on an optimized process, (2) reduce the time for design and troubleshooting by integrating process and device scale simulations to better predict performance and more effectively resolve issues, (3) quantify technical risk to enable more focused scale up activities, and finally, (4) stabilize the costs during commercial deployment by having a more comprehensive understanding of the process and underlying behavior of the system. This paper will provide an overview of the program and highlight recent accomplishments applying the tools to potential carbon capture technologies.

topic: The Four Dimensional Product: Integration Over Time Is the Only Way to Understand Sustainability
title: The Four Dimensional Product: Integration Over Time Is the Only Way to Understand Sustainability
authors_text: William Banholzer and Mark E. Jones
abstract: Sustainability is a question of time, integrating knowledge of production, use and end-of-life. Far too often, hype has surpassed reality, boundary conditions have been neglected and actions taken that don’t truly lead to a sustainable future. Singular focus on attributes like renewable content or biodegradability gives the wrong answer. Quality engineering forms the foundation for any meaningful discussion of sustainability, providing insights into energy and material flows, energy return, and thermodynamic constraints. The chemical industry is increasing resource and energy efficiency through innovation in both products and processes. Our mastery of materials science enables unique energy producing and energy saving products, products that improve sustainability by being significantly better than the next best alternatives during use.

topic: Maximization of Energy Efficiency of a Combined Heat and Power Plant
title: Maximization of Energy Efficiency of a Combined Heat and Power Plant
authors_text: Thomas F. Edgar, Kody Powell, Jong Kim and Kriti Kapoor
abstract: Energy efficiency is receiving increased attention as a way to reduce the use of fossil fuels and the resulting production of greenhouse gases. Automation, process control, and real-time optimization are key technologies to operate plants in the most efficient way. A combined heat and power plant at the University of Texas at Austin has been studied in order to reduce its carbon footprint as well as reduce costs. The steam power plant has been modeled using steady state mass and energy balances. Chillers have also been modeled so that their efficiencies can be maximized. There is also a thermal storage tank for chilled water to be used during periods of high demand. Forecasting of loads as well as the effect of weather have been incorporated into the real-time optimization approach. The effects of time of day pricing of power and use of demand response techniques to flatten demand curves are discussed. Usage of thermal energy storage along with automatic control gives additional degrees of freedom to deal with dynamic power conditions.

topic: Pan American Issues on Biofuel Sustainability
title: Pan American Issues on Biofuel Sustainability
abstract: Biofuels are in rapid development in many Pan American countries, yet the nature and extent of impacts on social and environmental systems from large-scale biofuel development are not well understood. This talk will explore sustainability issues across a broad set of impacts and in different Pan American countries and will begin to outline important research gaps. A future research agenda to overcome these knowledge gaps would help establish a new and growing biofuels industry onto a sustainable path.
